# buttermilk

> buttermilk is a predicate-based router for JavaScript. A route is `{ match, render }`, where `match` is a predicate returning `Params | null`. Predicates are typed and compose via `and`/`or`. The core is framework-agnostic; React 19 bindings are a separate package. A radix-tree compiler matches in sub-microsecond time; a linear `findRoute` oracle is also exported for strict first-match semantics.

This file is a cheatsheet and best-practices guide for LLMs and tools assisting humans who are using buttermilk. If you only read one section, read "Route shape" and "When to use which matcher".

## Packages

- `buttermilk` — framework-agnostic core.
- `buttermilk-react` — React 19 bindings. Peer-depends on `react@^19` and `react-dom@^19`.
- `buttermilk-react/server` — RSC-safe helpers (React.cache-memoized).

Both ship as ESM only. Node 20+.

```sh
npm i buttermilk                          # core only
npm i buttermilk-react react react-dom    # React 19 bindings
```

## Route shape

```ts
import { path, and, or, query, guard, regex, predicate } from 'buttermilk';

type Route = {
  match: Predicate;                          // Params | null
  render: (m: MatchResult) => unknown;       // framework-agnostic return
  redirect?: string | ((m: MatchResult) => string);
};
```

A predicate is a tagged union:

- `path('/users/:id')` — path pattern. `:name` captures one non-empty segment. `*` matches exactly one segment (no capture). `**` matches remaining segments and must be last. Invalid patterns (e.g. `**` not final, duplicate param names) throw at call time with an explicit message.
- `regex(/^\/files\/(?<year>\d{4})$/)` — RegExp against the pathname. Named capture groups become params.
- `query('q')` — requires the given key in the query string. The matched value becomes a typed param.
- `guard((req) => boolean)` — contributes no params; pure predicate gate.
- `predicate<T>((req) => T | null)` — user-typed escape hatch. Pass the params type via the generic.
- `and(a, b)` — both must match; param types intersect.
- `or(a, b)` — first match wins; param types union.

Aliases for terser hand-typing: `p` ≡ `path`, `custom` ≡ `predicate`. New code should prefer the long names.

## Typed params (never widen)

```ts
import type { ParamsOf } from 'buttermilk';

const pred = and(path('/users/:id'), query('tab'));
type P = ParamsOf<typeof pred>;  // { id: string; tab: string }
```

`ParamsOf` flows through template-literal path inference, `and` (→ intersection), and `or` (→ union). Do not annotate route renders with `Record<string, string>` — let inference work.

## When to use which matcher

- `findRoute(routes, req)` — linear first-match. Use for small tables, for strict first-match semantics across opaque (`custom`) predicates, or as the correctness oracle in tests.
- `compile(routes).find(req)` — radix-tree compiled router. Use for apps with many routes, or whenever match cost is measurable. Behavior matches `findRoute` for every URL the trie can handle; opaque predicates fall back to linear.

```ts
import { compile } from 'buttermilk';
const router = compile(routes);
const hit = router.find({ url: '/users/42' });
if (hit) hit.route.render(hit.result);
```

A `RouteRequest` is `{ url: string; method?: string; headers?: Record<string, string> }`.

## React 19 usage

```tsx
import { Router, Link, useParams, p } from 'buttermilk-react';

function User() {
  const { id } = useParams<{ id: string }>();
  return <h1>user {id}</h1>;
}

const routes = [
  { match: path('/'),          render: () => <Home /> },
  { match: path('/users/:id'), render: () => <User /> },
  { match: path('/**'),        render: () => <NotFound /> },
];

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Router routes={routes}>
      <Link href="/users/42">go</Link>
    </Router>
  );
}
```

Hooks are client-only. Calling any of them from a Server Component throws a teaching error that points at the file missing `'use client'`. All require a `<Router>` ancestor:

- `useRoute()` → active `MatchResult | null`.
- `useParams<P>()` → typed params. Throws if no route matched.
- `useLocation()` → parsed `Location` (`pathname`, `search`, `hash`, lazy `query`).
- `useNavigate()` → `(url: string) => void`.
- `useRouter()` → `{ url, result, route, navigate }`.

## React Server Components

`<Router>` and `<Link>` are isomorphic — the same `buttermilk-react` import works from a Server Component or a Client Component. Under React's `react-server` condition the module swaps in stateless implementations at load time: `<Router>` matches synchronously from a required `url` prop and `<Link>` emits a plain `<a href>`. Hooks stay client-only and throw a teaching error if called from a Server Component.

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx — Server Component, no 'use client' needed.
import { headers } from 'next/headers';
import { Router, Link } from 'buttermilk-react';
import { routes } from './routes';

export default async function Layout() {
  const url = (await headers()).get('x-url') ?? '/';
  return (
    <Router routes={routes} url={url}>
      <nav><Link href="/users/42">go</Link></nav>
    </Router>
  );
}
```

For match inspection without rendering — e.g. reading the matched route in a Server Component to set a data attribute — `buttermilk-react/server` exports `React.cache()`-wrapped helpers:

```ts
import { getRouteMatch, getPathname, getParams, getLocation } from 'buttermilk-react/server';
```

Every helper is wrapped in `React.cache()`, so repeated calls within a single render reuse work.

## Browser-optimized bundle

`buttermilk-react` ships a `browser`-condition entry (`dist/index.browser.mjs`) that drops RSC code paths entirely and is minified. Vite, webpack, and esbuild resolve it automatically when building for the browser. The isomorphic bundle remains under `default` and `react-server`. Nothing to configure at the app level — the correct entry is chosen by the resolver.

## SSR and controlled navigation

`<Router url="/users/42">` renders the given URL without touching browser history — use this for the initial server-rendered payload, then drop the prop on hydration so the client takes over history.

## Best practices by scenario

### Small table, simple paths (<20 routes)

Use `findRoute`. Skip `compile`. The linear scan is fine and reads straightforwardly.

### Medium-to-large table (~100–10 000 routes)

Use `compile(routes)`. Share the compiled router per process; do not re-compile per request.

### Auth gates

Compose `guard` with a path:

```ts
{ match: and(path('/admin/**'), guard((r) => r.headers?.cookie?.includes('sid='))),
  render: () => <Admin />,
  redirect: '/login' }
```

`redirect` may be a string or `(match) => string`.

### Query-driven routes

`query('q')` requires the key to exist and captures its value as `params.q`. Combine with a path via `and`:

```ts
and(path('/search'), query('q'))
```

### One-off predicate (feature flag, cookie, A/B)

`guard(req => bool)` if you contribute no params; `predicate<T>(req => T | null)` if you want typed data in `render`.

```ts
predicate<{ experiment: 'a' | 'b' }>((r) => {
  const flag = r.headers?.cookie?.match(/exp=(\w+)/)?.[1];
  return flag === 'a' || flag === 'b' ? { experiment: flag } : null;
})
```

### RSC + client hybrid

Match in a Server Component via `getRouteMatch(routes, url)` to branch layouts, then render a client-only `<Router>` only where interactivity is needed. Keep the route table in a file that both server and client import — matching is pure.

## Things v3 does not do

- No built-in scroll restoration. You own `scrollTo` calls in your render or via `useEffect` on `useLocation()`.
- No data loading / action story. buttermilk only matches; use your data layer (RSC, React Query, Suspense + `use()`) inside the rendered component.
- No nested-layout API distinct from JSX nesting. Layouts are just components that wrap children.
- No CJS build. Modern bundlers and Node 20+ resolve ESM natively.

## Differences from v2 (breaking)

- `*` used to be loose; now matches exactly one segment. `**` is new and matches the remainder (must be last). `:param` no longer captures empty segments.
- Route shape is `{ match, render }` instead of `{ path, render }`.
- React bindings live in `buttermilk-react`, not `buttermilk`.
- React 19 required. `prop-types`, `react-is`, `lite-url` removed.
- CJS dropped.

See https://buttermilk.js.org/migrating for the full guide.

## API reference (short)

```
buttermilk
  path(pattern)          // alias: p
  regex(re)              // named groups become params
  query(key)             // presence + value capture
  guard(fn)              // no params
  predicate<T>(fn)       // typed escape hatch; alias: custom
  and(a, b)              // intersection
  or(a, b)               // union
  findRoute(routes, req)
  compile(routes) -> { find(req) }
  parseUrl(url)
  matchPredicate(pred, req, loc)
  matchRoute(route, req)

  type Predicate, Route, RouteRequest, MatchResult, Location,
       ExtractParams<S>, ParamsOf<P>, CompiledRouter

buttermilk-react
  <Router routes url? compiled?>
  <Link href {...anchorProps}>
  useRouter(), useRoute(), useParams<P>(), useLocation(), useNavigate()
  (re-exports all of buttermilk above)

buttermilk-react/server
  getRouteMatch(routes, url)
  getPathname(url)
  getParams(routes, url)
  getLocation(url)
```
